newsitem.title: UK: Blast near British army HQ in N.Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Blast near British army HQ in N.Ireland.

text.p: Several people were injured when two suspected bombs exploded inside Britain's Northern Ireland army headquarters at Lisburn, south of Belfast, on Monday.
Security sources said they believed the blasts, which could be heard 10 miles (16 km) away in Belfast, had been caused by bombs but police said they were investigating the cause.
Police said there were several injuries.
Five casualties were being treated at the Lagan Valley Hospital nearby but hospital spokesman James Livingstone said it had been warned to expected upwards of 20.
Some other injured were being taken to a Belfast hospital, residents said.
The exact number of soldiers at the base is secret.
Army spokesmen said black smoke hung over the base after two explosions, one of which was very loud.
Police said no bomb warning had been given by any of Northern Ireland's feuding guerrilla groups and there was no immediate claim of responsibility.

Sky News reporter Gary Honeyford said: "We were waiting outside the Maze prison when we heard two blasts. We immediately made our way over there and as we approached the barracks there were two thick black plumes of smoke.
"Nobody immediately knew what the cause was but there were a lot of people looking distressed standing around the gates."

Northern Ireland has been largely immune from violence since rival guerrilla groups called ceasefires in 1994 but the Irish Republican Army (IRA) went back to war against British rule with attacks on British mainland targets in February.
It has avoided targets in Northern Ireland for fear of provoking a backlash by Protestant "Loyalist" guerrillas fighting to maintain British rule of the province, security sources believe.

Police chiefs say that any IRA attack in Northern Ireland itself would provoke retaliation by Loyalists who could also target the Irish Republic, which they accuse of backing the IRA goal of reuniting the two Irelands.

Last week police found a car bomb packed with explosives in Belfast and a breakaway Irish Republican group fighting British rule claimed reponsibility for planting the device, which failed to detonate.
